title: CLO 2025 Academic Month  Digital Empowerment of Apparel Engineering Teaching Resource Development
description: CLO 2025 Official Academic Monthly Course Review Now Available! Teacher Ma Kai from Beijing Institute of Fashion Technology shares online insights on the development of BIFT’s Fashion Engineering major, curriculum design, and talent cultivation teaching experiences.
transcript:
Good evening to all Close enthusiasts, digital fashion fans, fellow teachers, and students.

I am Ma Kai, a teacher from the School of Fashion Art and Engineering at Beijing Institute of Fashion Technology.  
Today, I am honored to share and exchange ideas with you.  
My topic is "Digital Empowerment in the Construction of Teaching Resources for Fashion Engineering."

I will share from four aspects: professional development, course construction, teaching resource development, and talent cultivation outcomes.

First, digital demand guides professional development.  
Let me first introduce the development history of the Fashion Design Engineering major at BIFT.  
The Fashion Design Engineering major was established in 1987 and was authorized to grant master's degrees in 1990.  
In 2009, it was approved by the Ministry of Education as one of the fourth batch of distinctive majors in national higher education institutions.  
In 2017, our school carried out cluster course construction and modular course reform.  
In 2019, it was selected as a first-class undergraduate major construction site and key first-class major in Beijing.  
In 2020, it was approved as a national first-class undergraduate major construction site.  
To meet the societal and industry demand for digital fashion design and technical talent, in 2019, we launched an experimental class for Digital Fashion Design, adopting a secondary selection process after admission.  
In 2024, last year, we upgraded the experimental digital class into a digital experimental class, emphasizing artificial intelligence and related skills cultivation.  
Here, I briefly show the basic curriculum plans for the regular Fashion Engineering class, the Digital Experimental class, and the upgraded Digital Experimental class, including graduation credits and training objectives.  
If you skim through this, you can see that the training objectives have changed in terms of students’ basic capabilities, future career directions, the competencies they should have upon graduation, and the industries they may engage in.

Talking about professional construction might feel abstract, so next, I will introduce how digital technology promotes course construction.  
Since we aim to cultivate digital talents, we have added some courses and improved others based on existing ones.  
In our curriculum, you can see distinctions between the regular Fashion Engineering class, the Digital Class, and the Digital Experimental Class regarding core courses.  
For example, starting from the Digital Class, we added Digital Fashion Simulation Technology, mainly focusing on practical 3D garment simulation operations.  
In the Digital Fashion Engineering class, we further added courses related to aesthetics such as Basic Art, and computer science fundamentals like Introduction to Computer Science, among others.  
There are many changes in the core professional courses.  
At that time, one important employment direction for the Digital Class was digital communication, including gaming and film and television sectors.  
Therefore, core courses included Virtual Character Design and Presentation, 3D Modeling, etc.  
In the new Digital Experimental Class, the focus shifted back to the fashion industry but incorporated courses on artificial intelligence, big data, and related content.

Overall, I summarize the curriculum design philosophy into five points:  
First, solidify mathematical and scientific fundamentals;  
second, enhance aesthetic ability;  
third, root in the fashion industry and emphasize professional practice;  
fourth, cultivate digital literacy.  
This was the overall curriculum concept proposed when we built the Digital Experimental Class last year, based on the demands of Beijing’s fashion industry.

You can see that compared to the regular class, the Digital Class and Digital Experimental Class have significant differences in core courses.  
The overall approach is to strengthen the foundation based on mathematics and science.  
We enhanced courses like Advanced Mathematics, Programming, and Introduction to Computer Science to strengthen mathematical foundations.  
Regarding aesthetic ability, we made Chinese and foreign fashion history compulsory and added Basic Art as a required course because students admitted to the Digital Class lacked an art background, so we increased this area overall.  
In professional practice, we added project-based practical courses.  
In digital literacy, we introduced courses related to artificial intelligence and others.

In the construction of digital technology courses, we achieved some results.  
For example, the course Fashion Digital Technology, jointly developed by Teacher Jiang Yan and myself, was awarded as one of the first batch of national-level first-class online courses in November 2020.  
In 2022, it was launched on the "Xuexi Qiangguo" platform and selected as a pilot course under the Expansion Plan.  
Later, we summarized the experiences of online course construction and applied for the "Textile Light" Teaching Achievement Award from the China Textile Federation and won the special prize.  
Additionally, our traditional digital course, Fashion CAD Application, led by our dean Gui Liang along with myself and other teachers, was approved in 2023 as the second batch of national first-class hybrid (online and offline) courses.  
These are some of the efforts we made in course construction.

Since these are digital courses, the digital aspect has inspired our teaching resource construction significantly.  
Traditionally, teaching resources mainly included class notes and textbooks.  
Now, with hybrid first-class digital courses, digital technology support enables us to make teaching resource construction more three-dimensional and comprehensive.  
First, I want to thank the leadership of our school for their support.  
When we started building the Digital Experimental Class in 2019, we renovated our computer labs and created a smart lab.  
Here is the hardware configuration of our lab.  
You might think the configuration is not high-end, but remember this was built in 2019, so even now, it remains quite robust.  
Students in the Digital Experimental Class use this hardware for their graduation projects, whether for digital garment simulation or post-production like video rendering; it works well.

Besides hardware, we actively cooperate with high-quality teaching platforms during the teaching process.  
For example, we use the “Yuketang” (Yangtze River Yuketang) platform for interactive classroom teaching.  
Especially in practical sessions, I use Yuketang’s video live streaming.  
After class, students can watch recorded sessions on the WeChat mini-program for review and reinforcement.  
On the Zhihui Shu (Smart Art) teaching platform, we have developed several flipped courses such as Fashion Digital Technology, Digital Fashion Simulation Technology, Fashion CAD Application, and a 3D Fashion Simulation course for graduate students.  
Students can easily browse the teaching resources I upload, including PPTs, teaching materials, practical materials, and operation videos on this platform.

I want to emphasize that starting this semester, I began using the Closet workspace for teaching applications.  
Some teachers and students watching this video might have used Closet in teaching or training before.  
During Closet training, our instructors used the workspace to grade assignments, which interested me greatly.  
With support from Closet company, our school was granted high-level permissions to use Closet.  
Since this semester, I have used Closet in courses such as Digital Fashion Simulation Technology, the Experimental Class, Design Class, and minor courses in Fashion Engineering.  
Students can easily download materials and submit assignments there.  
For teachers, when students submit project files, I can directly comment inside the Closet workspace without opening the software.  
I often use the annotation feature to mark problematic parts in students’ work, so they know exactly where issues occur upon opening their files.  
I also use the workflow feature on the left side of each student’s project file to mark assignment grades.  
For example, works that are good and need no modification are marked as “adopt.”  
Those requiring revision are marked in gray.  
In the lower-left corner, there are options for workflow and grading, making it clear to students about their assignment status and grades, which I find very convenient.

Additionally, since our school recently completed teaching evaluations last semester, archiving 3D assignments is challenging for many teachers.  
Closet’s comment feature allows us to export submitted project files directly into Excel, which includes students’ personal information and their three-view drawings.  
This makes archiving and submitting to experts easier.  
You can also convert the Excel file to PDF to reduce file size.  
Of course, project files can be downloaded directly but the speed is slower.  
From an archiving perspective, this method is very convenient.  
I encourage teachers interested in digital fashion to try using Closet.

Please turn to the next slide.

Besides these teaching resource attempts, we also focus on MOOCs and micro-course development.  
Around 2019, we launched two MOOCs on the XueTang Online platform: Fashion Digital Technology and Fashion CAD Application.  
Fashion Digital Technology now has over 30,000 enrolled students.  
Fashion CAD Application has more than 6,000 students and over 20 sessions offered.  
Later, our school developed MOOCs in fashion craft courses, fashion product planning and design, fashion design effect drawing, etc., using the Chinese University MOOCs platform.

Due to rapid technological updates in digital fashion, MOOCs may not update quickly enough.  
Therefore, I created a personal account on Bilibili.  
If you search for Teacher Ma Kai from BIFT on Bilibili, you will find my account.  
It contains some case operation videos used in class.

Please turn to the next slide.

Next, I want to talk about an important topic: textbook construction.  
Normally, we use printed textbooks, but for technologies like digital fashion and other courses, there is a new form called “new form textbooks” or “digital textbooks.”  
These are supported by our school’s Academic Affairs Office under textbook project approvals.  
For example, I am the chief editor of a textbook titled Digital Fashion Simulation Technology, published in September 2024.  
Students and teachers can find it on the “Cloud Textbook” app or download the PC version.  
This book differs from traditional paper textbooks by including many multimedia files such as high-definition images and videos.  
Images can be viewed in various gallery forms, and videos are easy to edit, making it user-friendly.

In this textbook, I integrate some advantages of teaching materials.  
Each chapter includes teaching suggestions such as learning objectives and educational goals.  
Unlike other digital fashion textbooks that mainly demonstrate operations and cases, I also include a lot of theoretical content.  
Therefore, this book is a 14th Five-Year Plan textbook.  
Teachers needing such materials may pay attention to it.

Additionally, this textbook incorporates AI applications.  
If you download it, you can use its built-in intelligent agent to generate lesson plans, teaching plans, test questions, and more, which is very helpful for teachers.

Please turn to the next slide.

Please turn to the next slide.

Another textbook I co-edited with Teacher Jiang Yan is Fashion Digital Technology.  
We published a printed version in 2023, but considering the user base and the benefits of digital formats, we revised and released it as a digital textbook.

Please turn to the next slide.

Additionally, we developed course knowledge maps for Digital Fashion Simulation Technology and Fashion Big Data courses.  
These were created on the Zhihui Shu platform, supported by an interdisciplinary project in our school related to fashion studies.  
We aimed to design knowledge maps for several courses to facilitate logical curriculum review and provide good recommendations for course cluster construction.  
These knowledge maps are excellent teaching resources, helping students organize their thinking clearly.  
Learning is not random but systematic, starting from one knowledge point and expanding to similar points, making learning more structured.

Please turn to the next slide.

Finally, let’s look at some training outcomes for digital fashion talents.

Please turn to the next slide.

In the past two years, our students have participated in online school courses.  
You can scan the QR code to visit these courses.  
Here is a comprehensive display of students’ homework, including pictures and design descriptions.

Please turn to the next slide.

This is a detailed display of student projects.

Please turn to the next slide.

This set of works is themed on wedding dresses.  
Students performed well.  
I incorporated several images from their digital teaching into our curriculum.

Now I will translate for you.

Please turn to the next slide.

This is another course, Digital Costume and Overall Design 1, mainly taught by Mr. Yu Xizi.  
They also participated in the course presentation.  
Scan the QR code on the left to see more information.

Please turn to the next slide.

Digital Costume and Overall Design 1 was designed by Mr. Yu Xizi.  
The course is intended for students entering the second year next semester.  
In the next semester, students will be able to design comprehensive works, broadening their thinking beyond the main theme.

Please turn to the next slide.

The second phase of Digital Fashion Comprehensive Design focuses more on character design based on the first phase.  
These are some student works.

Please turn to the next slide.

The third phase is more advanced.  
Students form groups to create a brand, conduct research, design products and related items, and produce promotional videos.

Please turn to the next slide.

This is the work from our first digital fashion graduating class in 2023.  
The graduation show included three types of design themes: Cyberpunk, National Trend, and Natural Mirror.  
This video corresponds to the first theme and shows real garments on the runway and digital garments.

Please turn to the next slide.

Next, the digital fashion class will be divided into two groups.

Please turn to the next slide.

Because the works are not officially released, I selected smaller images.  
If you want to see more beautiful digital costumes, you can attend our digital exhibition on the 28th of this month at 2:30 p.m. at the Beijing International Dressing Room near Tongzhou New School.  
You are warmly welcome to join.

Besides costume design, our students have achieved academic results in digitalization, such as research on foldable art applications in digital costumes and virtual art of 3D and close 3D embroidery.  
Thank you.

Regarding embroidery, we developed new methods based on the PBR (Physically Based Rendering) process to achieve embroidery effects.  
Most research focuses on digitalizing traditional costume craftsmanship.

Please turn to the next slide.

Here we show some student research outcomes, such as costume detail design, smart customization systems, ancient costume restoration platforms, and final demonstrations.

On the far right, students participated in the Beijing Cultural and Art Foundation Project in 2023, commemorating its 100th anniversary.  
Our students contributed digital works to this project.

Finally, on this page, we show student participation in related competitions, mainly the Future Designers Digital Costume Art Design Competition.  
Our students have won several awards, including third prize nationwide and first, second, and third prizes in Beijing.  
Due to limited space, only some awards are listed.

That concludes my introduction. Thank you.
